cards.text: The people of Zion are speaking together, as one big "we," straight to the LORD. Enemies have come through Jerusalem's gates, and fire has burned Zion down to its foundations (Lamentations 4:11-12). So they bring the whole thing to Him in one long, honest prayer.

cards.question: Before they say anything else, what do the people of Zion ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Remember what has happened to them
Punish Edom for all its sins
Send them a new king to lead

cards.text: Then they start listing what they've lost, one thing at a time. First up: the land and the houses their families handed down.

cards.question: The people of Zion say their family land and their houses now belong to strangers and foreigners.

cards.text: Then it gets personal. They say they've become fatherless orphans, and their mothers are widows.

cards.question: Water. The people of Zion have to PAY for water now. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for years, and even the dust was free. What else comes at a price for them?

cards.text: They're closely pursued and weary, and they find no rest. And just to get enough bread, they gave themselves over to two other nations.

cards.question: To get enough bread, which two nations did the people of Zion submit to?

cards.text: Then they look back at the generation that came before them. Those people are gone now, but somebody is still paying for what they did.

cards.question: The people of Zion say: Our ___ sinned and are no more, but we bear their ___.

cards.text: And who's in charge over them now? They say slaves rule over them.

cards.question: The people of Zion say someone is on the way to rescue them from the hands of those who rule over them.

cards.text: Even getting bread is dangerous now. They get it at the risk of their lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.

cards.question: The hunger has the people of Zion burning with fever. This next picture comes from my world, friend. Their skin, they say, is as hot as ___.

cards.text: The hurt reaches everyone. Women have been ravished in Zion and in the cities of Judah, and princes have been hung up by their hands.

cards.question: In Zion, the elders still receive respect from the people.

cards.text: Not even the young are spared. The boys stagger under loads of wood.

cards.question: And the young men of Zion? What are they stuck doing?

cards.text: The elders have left the city gate. And the young men have stopped their music.

cards.question: Joy has left the hearts of the people of Zion, and their dancing has turned to ___.

cards.text: They say the crown has fallen from their head. Now, remember earlier, when they said their fathers sinned?

cards.question: Now the people of Zion say they have sinned too, not only their fathers.

cards.text: Because of all this, their hearts are faint and their eyes grow dim.

cards.question: The people of Zion say their eyes grow dim because of Mount Zion. What has happened to it?

answers.text: It's been handed over to Edom

cards.text: The only ones patrolling Mount Zion now are foxes. Walking their rounds like night security at a building nobody visits anymore. Then the whole prayer turns, and they start talking about the LORD Himself.

cards.question: When the prayer turns, what do the people of Zion say about the LORD and His throne?

answers.text: He reigns forever and His throne endures
He left His throne when the city fell
His throne now sits in a far country

cards.question: Right after praising the LORD's forever throne, the people of Zion still ask Him why He has forgotten them and forsaken them for so long.

cards.text: Then comes the big ask, the one this whole prayer has been building to. They want to come back to the LORD.

cards.question: The people of Zion ask the LORD to ___ them to Himself, so they may ___.

cards.text: And they ask Him to renew their days as of old. Friend, I was a worn-out stamper in the back of a junk drawer, and the One they're praying to made me NEW. I know a little something about that prayer.

cards.question: The prayer of the people of Zion ends with every question settled and every fear gone.

cards.text: The very last line is an honest one: "unless You have utterly rejected us and remain angry with us beyond measure." They bring even that fear straight to the LORD.

findings.problem: The setup says the people are listing what they've 'lost', starting with the land and houses. That already tells the baker the land and houses are no longer theirs, so the true-or-false on card 4 (now owned by strangers and foreigners) is answered before it's asked, and 'False' is ruled out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This choice card brings in a new moment of the passage itself (they have to pay for water) and a joke inside the question. The setup belongs on a story card, and the choice card should be one question and its answers.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The setup gives away both blanks on card 10. 'The generation that came before them' points straight to 'fathers', and 'somebody is still paying for what they did' points straight to 'punishment'. That rules out 'enemies', 'neighbors' and 'blessing'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'This next picture comes from my world, friend' points the baker to the bakery, so 'an oven' is given away and 'the sun' and 'a desert' are ruled out by the question itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Lamentations 5:11 says 'virgins in the cities of Judah', but the card says women were ravished 'in Zion and in the cities of Judah'. That changes what the text calls the second group.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Lamentations 5:12 says only that 'elders receive no respect'. It doesn't say from whom. The statement adds 'from the people', which names who is disrespecting the elders. A baker could argue the people still respect them even though their enemies don't.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences (the foxes, the night-security joke, and the turn of the prayer). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'They want to come back to the LORD' gives away the second blank on card 15 ('return') and rules out 'rest'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: For the first blank, 'punish' and 'scatter' don't fit '___ them to Himself'. Only 'restore' reads naturally in that line, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences (renew their days, his own renewal, and 'I know a little something about that prayer'). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'They bring even that fear straight to the LORD' states their feeling as fact. Lamentations 5:22 doesn't call it a fear. If Papa Dorin wants to name the feeling, it needs to be marked as his own guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: Many story cards are bare paraphrases with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples: stop 1 card 13, stop 2 card 5 ('The elders have left the city gate. And the young men have stopped their music.') and stop 2 card 9 ('Because of all this, their hearts are faint and their eyes grow dim.'). Across 32 cards, there are only two lighter moments (the free dust and the fox security guards).

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
